title.narrative: Building an active, networked civil society to improve delivery and access to quality education in Thailand

description.narrative: The action enhances the capacity of Thai CSOs to contribute to development and governance processes in Thailand, in particular those concerned with education, and the achievement of SDGs 1, 4, 5 and 10. Specifically, it will increase the technical, organisational and management capacity of 6 Thai CSO organisations and networks to play an effective role in the delivery of an equitable and quality education, with a focus on small schools in remote and marginalized areas.

comment.narrative: 6 of 6 CSOs AAT TEACA TBA KDEC and MKDEC reported increased in working on governance processes. At national level AAT and TEACA were successfully worked and partnered with the Office of the Education Council OEC in governance processes through national education assembly on June 20 2023. At local level TBA and KDEC increased facilitating activities in local governance processes with community school local authorities and primary education service areas offices located in Maha Sarakham and Roiet provinces. As the results new organization named Maha Sarakham Development Education Council MKDEC was established and have been promoting active learning innovation and small school management. Two more CSOs ISN and NSSAA increased working in governance as they were familiar with school management and community participation in terms of school governance. Correspondingly the external final evaluation findings found that 90 of communities where the SMCs reported participating in school meetings improving school governance in action plansactivities.

Secondly submitted policy recommendation on Small Schools Model as presented in a booklet named Policy Brief to Police General Permpoon Chidchob the Minister of Education was eventually organized.

By the end of 2023 the project reported that 467 schools were reached out as small school network where 183 schools in Central 62 schools in Northern 222 schools in Northeastern. Internal project monitoring survey presented that 93.94 of target schools described having an active multistakeholder partnership involving CSOs communities and LAs to support their schools initiatives. For instance target schools in Nan province provided information that communities members SMCs including LAs actively participated in school meetings and volunteered in activities. In additions to school governance target school directors started engaging SMCs LAs and CSOs when facing closure policy as threat led increased participation and partnerships from the community LAs and CSOs managing schools.
